1.say: Flip the black entry bedroom breaker handle to off in the panel.
placements: black entry bedroom breaker toggle → off side of the entry bedroom slot in the open breaker panel, pushed with fingertip on the plastic handle, in the video: middle column third breaker down labeled ENTRY BEDROOM 1 2, 15 amp Eaton breaker
watch_for: Flipping the wrong labeled breaker so the entry light still works when tested.
Leaving the handle halfway so power flickers and the toggle sits between on and off.
1.check_yourself: The labeled breaker toggle rests in the OFF position inside the open panel.
1.safety: Keep fingers on the plastic handle and clear of bare metal inside the panel.

2.say: Unscrew the four small cover screws from the white double plate. Lift the white rectangular cover straight off the wall switches.
placements: four small faceplate cover screws → out of the top and bottom holes of the white double cover beside the white door frame, removed with a cordless drill driver on each screw head, in the video: two screws above both white rockers and two screws below

white double rectangular faceplate → off the wall to expose both white rocker switches on the gray wall left of the door lock, lifted away by hand, in the video: cover removed beside the silver and black entry lock
watch_for: Prying the cover hard and chipping paint so white paint sticks to the plate edge.
Losing a tiny screw so the later cover rattles with an empty hole.
2.check_yourself: Two white switches are exposed on the wall with no cover.

3.say: Unscrew the two silver mounting screws from the right white switch. Pull the right white switch straight out of the blue wall box. Cut the two black wall wires free from the old switch body.
placements: two silver mounting screws on the right white old switch → out of the top and bottom metal tabs of the blue double wall box, removed with a small screwdriver on each screw head, in the video: right switch screws above and below the rocker

right white old switch body → pulled straight out of the right side of the blue wall box to hang on its wires left of the white door trim, pulled by hand, in the video: right side opening with left white switch still mounted

two black wall wires and bare ground wire → cut and unscrewed free from the old switch terminals with wire cutters on the copper near the switch body, leaving loose ends hanging, in the video: wires cut with the old switch held in the right hand
watch_for: Pulling the left working switch loose so the left rocker wobbles after.
Cutting wall wires too short so less than half an inch of bare wire shows.
3.check_yourself: One white switch remains mounted beside an open blue hole with loose wires hanging out.
3.safety: Confirm the breaker is off and keep cutter jaws away from fingers.

4.say: Twist the green switch wire to the bare ground wire in the box. Screw a yellow wire cap firmly over both bare ends.
placements: green insulated switch ground wire → twisted together with the bare copper ground wire hanging from the right side of the blue wall box, twisted by hand, in the video: joint hanging below the opening beside the left mounted white switch
yellow twist wire cap → screwed firmly clockwise over both ground ends until tight with no bare copper showing, twisted by hand, in the video: yellow cap hanging below the blue box opening
watch_for: Capping green to a black hot wire so the breaker trips when restored.
Leaving bare copper outside the yellow cap so copper glints below the cap.
4.check_yourself: A yellow cap joins the green switch wire to the bare ground wire hanging from the box.
4.safety: Keep the breaker off and do not touch bare copper ends.

5.say: Twist the white switch wire with the white wall wires in the box. Screw a yellow wire cap firmly over all white ends. Screw a second yellow cap onto the lone blue switch wire.
placements: white insulated smart switch neutral wire → twisted together with the bundled white neutral wall wires inside the blue box, twisted by hand, in the video: bundle on the right side of the opening near the left mounted white switch

yellow twist wire cap for neutrals → screwed clockwise over all white ends until tight with no bare copper showing, in the video: yellow cap closing the white bundle, narration says red cap but the finished frame shows yellow

short blue insulated switch wire → capped alone with a yellow twist wire cap screwed firmly over its end and left unused near the wall opening, in the video: lone blue wire with yellow cap hanging from the new switch
watch_for: Leaving one white wall wire out of the bundle so one white end hangs uncapped.
Leaving the blue wire uncapped so the bare copper tip shows with no yellow cap.
5.check_yourself: Yellow caps close the bundled white wires and the lone blue wire near the wall opening.
5.safety: Keep the breaker off while you twist bare wires together.

6.say: Strip about half an inch from both black wall wires. Join the black switch wire to one black wall wire under a yellow cap. Join the red switch wire to the other black wall wire under a yellow cap.
placements: two black insulated wall wires → stripped about half an inch of insulation from each end with cutters, in the video: stripped ends on the right side of the blue box

black insulated smart switch wire → twisted to one stripped black wall wire and closed with a yellow twist cap screwed tight with no copper showing, in the video: lower yellow capped joint hanging below the blue box beside the door

red insulated smart switch wire → twisted to the other stripped black wall wire and closed with a yellow twist cap screwed tight with no copper showing, in the video: middle yellow capped joint with red wire to black wire beside the blue box
watch_for: Leaving bare copper exposed below the yellow caps so copper shows and can short.
Mixing white neutrals with black hots so the switch stays dark and the breaker trips.
6.check_yourself: Yellow caps join the new switch black and red wires to the black wall wires.
6.safety: Keep the breaker off and keep black ends separated while you work.

7.say: Fold all capped wires neatly into the blue wall box. Push the white smart switch into the right side of the box. Drive the silver mounting screws into the top and bottom tabs.
placements: white smart switch body with metal mounting tabs → pushed into the right side of the blue double wall box beside the left old white switch with wires folded behind, pushed by hand, in the video: new switch on the right of the old switch in the open wall hole

two silver mounting screws → driven into the top and bottom tabs of the new switch with a cordless drill driver on each screw head until snug and flush, in the video: drill with light applied to the top and bottom screws of the right switch
watch_for: Trapping a wire under the metal tab so the switch sits crooked and not flush.
Overtightening so the rocker binds and sticks when pressed.
7.check_yourself: A new white smart switch sits mounted beside the old white switch in the open wall box.
7.safety: Tuck all bare ends inside before you turn the breaker back on.

8.say: Set the white double faceplate over both wall switches. Drive the small cover screws into the four plate holes.
placements: white double rectangular faceplate → set flat over both the left old white switch and the right new white smart switch on the gray wall left of the door, aligned by hand, in the video: plate covering the wall with both rockers visible and a small green light on the right switch

four small cover screws → driven into the top and bottom holes of the faceplate with a small screwdriver on each screw head until snug, in the video: two screws above and two screws below the two rockers beside the entry lock
watch_for: Covering the green indicator with the plate edge so the green light hides behind plastic.
Tightening one side more so the plate gaps and one edge lifts off the gray wall.
8.check_yourself: A white double faceplate covers the wall with both switches visible and a green light on.
8.safety: Keep fingers on the plastic plate and clear of live terminals.
